subject: POC trial: model selection, success criteria & kickoff
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial: model selection, success criteria & kickoff

Hey Alex / Sam —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap + proposed plan for the POC so we can align on success criteria, timeline, and which models to try during the trial. If anything below is off, flag it and I'll update.

Call recap (what I captured)
- Goal: Evaluate an on-prem / private POC of Redwood to power Acme's multilingual customer support classification + short-response suggestions.
- Primary success metrics: intent classification accuracy on labeled set, generation accuracy (factuality), latency P95 under 450ms for single-turn responses, operational cost target < $0.60 / 1k tokens (trial baseline).
- Data: You'll provide ~500 representative prompts across EN/ES/FR (balanced).

Proposed evaluation plan (high level)
1) Week 0 (this week): kick off, exchange datasets + access + NDA addendum (if needed).
2) Week 1: Redwood spins up trial endpoints, runs baseline tests on two candidate models.
3) Week 2: Ingest the 500 sample prompts, run evaluation harness (metrics: accuracy, hallucination %, latency p95, token cost), iterate prompt templates.
4) Week 3: Tune prompt templates, test fallback routing & caching; run multilingual stress tests.
5) Week 4: Results review, final recommendations, and next steps (Dedicated or Private).

Model selection (initial recommendation)
- Primary: Llama 2-13B Chat (q4_0 quantized) — balance of quality and multilingual coverage.
- Fallback: Mistral 7B Instruct (q4) — lower-latency fallback for high throughput requests.
- If we need stronger multilingual support (FR/ES heavy): run a candidate of MPT-7B-Chat or a FLAN variant for comparison.

Ownership
- Redwood AE (me) — program lead & outcomes coordination (Marissa).
- Redwood Solutions (Ben) — model selection, infra config, and evaluation harness.
- Acme — provide labeled test set and accept/reject decision for the POC.

Attachments: I attached a starter "POC-success-criteria.xlsx" and a short kickoff agenda.

Next weeks — proposed kickoff window: Mon 20 Jul or Tue 21 Jul (your preference).

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Redwood Inference — High-performance inference for production LLMs

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeinc.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmeinc.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection, success criteria & kickoff

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. That matches our notes. A few clarifications and requests: 

1) Success criteria tweaks:
- For classification, target > 88% accuracy on the labeled set.
- For generation (suggested responses), we need < 3% hallucination on our sample.
- Latency: P95 under 400ms would be ideal for our user experience; if not possible, we can relax to 450ms.

2) Dataset: we'll share the 500-sample set by end of Friday (link below). It's approximately 60% EN, 25% ES, 15% FR. We'll also include a small labeled validation set (~200 labels) for accuracy checks.

3) Model preference: we'd prefer to start with a smaller model for the trial to verify latency/cost first (e.g., Mistral 7B) and then compare to Llama 2-13B for quality. If you have quantized variants that preserve quality, that works.

4) Access: can your trial use a private subnet? We have security constraints — I'll loop in our security contact if needed.

We can do kickoff Tue 21 Jul 10am ET. Please send calendar invite.

Link to dataset (shared folder): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cACME-POC

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Customer Support Technology | Acme Inc.
alex.johnson@acmeinc.com | +1 (212) 555-0112

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeinc.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection, success criteria & kickoff

Thanks Alex — good adjustments. Technical notes from our side and a slightly updated model plan based on the latency/accuracy tradeoffs you called out: 

Quick approach
- We'll start the trial with Mistral-7B (q4_0) as the baseline to validate latency and cost targets.
- In parallel we'll run a Llama-2-13B Chat (q4_0) candidate on a small sample to compare quality.
- If you need stronger FR/ES coverage, we'll add an MPT-7B-Chat run for side-by-side comparison.

Config notes
- Quantization: use q4_0 for both models initially — it generally preserves quality while reducing memory and inference cost. We can test q4_1 / q5 if you want to trade memory for slightly different latency profiles.
- Routing: we'll configure smart routing so low-latency traffic prefers Mistral 7B; if confidence for classification is low (below threshold), route to Llama 2-13B for final scoring.
- Caching & batching: enable prefix KV caching for repeated prefixes; batch size tuned to keep P95 latency under 400ms.

Evaluation harness
- Ben (solutions) will run the evaluation harness on your 500 prompts + 200 labeled validation records. Metrics: classification accuracy, response correctness (binary), hallucination rate (manual spot checks), token/time cost, latency p50/p95, and throughput.

Security/Private subnet
- We can run the trial inside your VPC via Redwood Private (short-term trial instance) — we'll need an IP allowlist and an SSH key for bootstrap. If that's acceptable, I'll send a short checklist for your infra team.

Next actions
- Marissa: please send SOW draft / trial terms for signatures.
- Alex: confirm Tue 21 Jul 10am ET kickoff and share an infra contact for the VPC work.
- Ben: I'll prepare the evaluation harness and baseline run plan.

I've attached a short kickoff agenda and a starter POC-success-criteria spreadsheet so we can populate numerical thresholds.


Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (650) 555-0233
